- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) and forecast is high, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid over-optimism.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤0.3) and forecast is low, increase forecast by 5–10% to counteract pessimism.  
- After a sharp price spike, model tends to overcorrect downward; delay the drop by 1–2 periods and reduce magnitude.  
- Model often overestimates mean reversion in short-term (1–3 days) — adjust downward by 2–5% if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if last 3–5 days show strong downward momentum + negative sentiment, model tends to underestimate — add 3–7% to forecast.  
- If sentiment is volatile or mixed (±0.3–0.6), model overfits recent trends — smooth forecast by averaging last 5–7 days.  
- When sentiment is consistently positive over 3+ days, model tends to overpredict — apply a 5–10% downward bias.  
- If forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average and sentiment is neutral, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid momentum bias.
